title: Listen to a tech talk and write a summary (B2)
summary: Listen to a short tech talk with a host and Q&A, then write a summary of the claims, evidence and what you would try.
learningObjectives: Follow the structure of a short technical talk
Write a summary with what you would try next

turns.text: Welcome back. Our next talk is about slow builds. Victor leads the developer tools team at a mid-size company, and he will share what they changed last year. Victor, the floor is yours.

Thanks, Hana. A year ago, our full build took twenty-two minutes. People stopped running it locally, so bugs reached the shared branch. We made three changes. First, we cached dependencies between runs. Second, we ran tests in parallel. Third, we only rebuilt the parts that changed.

The result was a median build of six minutes. The biggest gain came from the third change, which saved about eight of those sixteen minutes. Caching saved four, and parallel tests saved the rest. I should be honest: we measured on our main branch for one month, and our monorepo is quite large, so your numbers may differ.
Thank you, Victor. We have time for one question.
Thanks for the talk. Did you see any problems with cached dependencies, for example old versions that stayed in the cache?
Yes, once. A cache entry kept an old library version and a test passed when it should have failed. Now the cache key includes the lock file hash, so any change in dependencies creates a new entry.
That makes sense. If I wanted to try this, where would you start?
Measure first. Find the slowest step, then change one thing at a time. In our case, rebuilding only changed parts was the best start, but it needs a clear map of dependencies, so give it time.
Great advice. Thank you again, Victor, and thanks to everyone for listening.

performanceTask.title: Write a talk summary
performanceTask.scenario: After a tech talk, you write a short summary for your team with what you would try.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: From the rough notes of a tech talk, write a summary in English (60 to 110 words): claims, evidence, a limitation and what you would try. Do not look at the model answer yet.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Write a talk summary in English, 60 to 110 words: the main claim, the evidence, one limitation and the first thing you would try.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Talk summary: faster builds. Victor argued that rebuilding only changed parts of the code helps most. As evidence, he said the median build dropped from twenty-two to six minutes after three changes: caching dependencies, running tests in parallel and rebuilding only what changed. The third change saved about eight minutes. One limitation is that the data covers one month on one large repository, so our results may differ. He also warned that cache keys must include the lock file hash. I would start by measuring our slowest build step, then change one thing at a time.
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Write the summary again in English. Keep the structure and make the evidence more precise.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: Write a summary of a different talk, such as one about code reviews.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Write a summary of another talk without looking at old notes.

anchors.met: The reader sees the claim, numbers, a limitation and a next step.
anchors.notMet: Evidence or the limitation is missing.

rubric.label: Accurate reporting
rubric.description: The summary reports what the speaker said.

anchors.met: Numbers and claims match the talk.
anchors.notMet: Numbers are wrong or the speaker is misquoted.

rubric.label: Reporting verbs
rubric.description: Uses verbs such as argued, showed and warned.

anchors.met: Uses at least three different reporting verbs.
